result:
I would institute universal, involuntary empathy: the direct, physical and emotional experience of the impact your actions have on others. 

If a person inflicts suffering, they would feel that exact pain in real time. If they hoard resources while someone starves, they would feel the physical distress of that hunger. Conversely, if they alleviate suffering or bring relief, they would feel the surge of that comfort.

Most of the world's cruelty and destruction relies on distance—geographical, social, or psychological. War, exploitation, extreme greed, and neglect all require the ability to disconnect from the human cost of one's choices. 

By removing the luxury of detachment, self-interest and the collective good would become the same thing. You wouldn't need to persuade people to be good; cause and effect would be inescapable.
